note: MEK inhibition downstream of KRAS regressed pancreatic xenografts and gave KRAS-driven mice only modest gains, yet four randomised trials (selumetinib, trametinib, refametinib, pimasertib) found no survival benefit.
label: Pancreatic cancer (MEK)

engagement.note: Selumetinib blocked ERK phosphorylation in xenografts and PBMCs; no pancreatic trial has reported on-treatment tumour pERK.
engagement.short: pERK blocked in xenografts, never read in patients
engagement.quote: When dosed orally, ARRY-142886 was capable of inhibiting both ERK1/2 phosphorylation and growth of HT-29 xenograft tumors in nude mice.
engagement.reason: No on-treatment pERK in pancreatic patients
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level read. The pERK read-out in Yeh 2007 was HT-29 (colon) xenografts and TPA-stimulated PBMCs; the pancreatic BxPC3 model is reported for growth only. The only pancreatic-trial pERK measurement found was baseline archival IHC in the CI-1040 phase II (Rinehart 2004, doi:10.1200/JCO.2004.01.185), not on-treatment engagement. Lito 2014 (doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2014.03.011) showed in models that MEK inhibitors suppress ERK less in KRAS-mutant than BRAF-mutant tumours (CRAF-mediated reactivation), but no pancreatic patient comparison of that prediction was published.

efficacy.note: Selumetinib regressed BxPC3 pancreatic xenografts; KRAS-mutant xenografts later regressed too (Hofmann 2012), the rationale for KRAS-mutant trials.
efficacy.quote: Tumor regressions were also seen in a BxPC3 xenograft model.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level read. BxPC3 is a KRAS wild-type line (outside knowledge, not stated in the abstract). The KRAS-mutant xenograft prediction is Hofmann 2012 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0044146, epub 2012-08-31): 'Tumors of all three models regressed upon MEK inhibition' with AZD6244; trametinib PDX work is Walters 2013 (doi:10.1593/neo.121712). Collisson 2012 (doi:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-11-0347) called MEK inhibition 'highly effective both in vivo and in vitro' in human PDA lines.

efficacy.note: Trametinib + gemcitabine: OS HR 0.98; KRAS-mutant subgroup (n=103) no difference, though KRAS-mutant xenografts had regressed on MEK inhibition.
efficacy.short: KRAS-mutant patients gained nothing from trametinib
efficacy.quote: KRAS mutation-positive patients (n=103) showed no difference in OS between arms.
efficacy.reason: Xenografts regressed; patients did not benefit
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level read (EJC paywalled); the KRAS-subgroup sentence is verbatim from the abstract. Year choice: earlier unselected failures exist, CI-1040 0/15 pancreatic responses (Rinehart 2004, doi:10.1200/JCO.2004.01.185) and selumetinib vs capecitabine OS 5.4 vs 5.0 months (Bodoky 2012, doi:10.1007/s10637-011-9687-4, epub 2011-05-19, NCT00372944, no registry results), but neither genotyped KRAS, so the first KRAS-mutant comparison is Infante 2014; move the contra to 2012 if unselected PDAC trials are accepted as proxies. Later same-direction results: refametinib + gemcitabine ORR/PFS/OS higher in patients WITHOUT detectable KRAS mutation (Van Laethem 2017, doi:10.1007/s11523-016-0469-y, NCT01251640, no registry results); pimasertib + gemcitabine no PFS/OS benefit, KRAS status irrelevant (Van Cutsem 2018, doi:10.1002/ijc.31603, NCT01016483, results posted 2017-06-23). The KRAS-driven GEMM (KPC-type) reported modest single-agent MEK tumour growth inhibition without survival gain (Junttila 2015, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-14-0030, epub 2014-11-05; Alagesan 2015, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-1591, epub 2014-10-27), both after Infante's 2014-06-07 epub, so a post-hoc match, not a prediction; the same GEMMs predicted MEK + PI3K combination benefit, and selumetinib + MK-2206 then gave shorter OS than mFOLFOX (3.9 vs 6.7 months; Chung 2017, doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2016.5383, NCT01658943, results posted 2016-03-09; MK-2206 is an AKT inhibitor, a class proxy for the PI3K inhibitors used in mice). Adaptive-resistance explanations (CRAF-mediated MEK reactivation, Lito 2014; PI3K/RTK rebound, Pettazzoni 2015, doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-14-1854; protective autophagy, Kinsey 2019, doi:10.1038/s41591-019-0367-9, which states 'inhibition of this pathway has provided no clinical benefit to patients with PDA') all post-date the failures. Kinsey's PDX-based trametinib + hydroxychloroquine prediction was itself contradicted: 13/13 evaluable patients progressed within 100 days in a retrospective cohort (Witte 2024, doi:10.1007/s00432-024-05954-5); the prospective THREAD trial NCT03825289 was terminated with no results posted.

safety.note: PDX papers report trametinib combinations as tolerated; no pancreatic trial compared mouse tolerability with patient toxicity (rash, diarrhoea, ocular, thrombocytopenia).
safety.short: Mouse tolerability never compared with patients
safety.quote: Dual antibody therapy in conjunction with trametinib was equally or more effective at inhibiting tumor growth and with lower apparent toxicity than trametinib plus lapatinib.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level read. The only safety statement from a pancreatic model found is a relative tolerability remark about trametinib combinations in PDX mice; the models made no prediction about the class toxicities patients showed (more thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea, rash, stomatitis and grade 3 anaemia with trametinib + gemcitabine, Infante 2014; ocular events 28.9% vs 4.8% with pimasertib + gemcitabine, Van Cutsem 2018; grade >=3 toxicity in 39 vs 23 patients with selumetinib + MK-2206 vs mFOLFOX, Chung 2017). No published comparison. Toxicology-species data sit in the trametinib melanoma NDA, outside this context.
